ImageDescription.value:
Surfers Paradise is a suburb in the City of Gold Coast, Queensland, Australia. In the 2021 census, Surfers Paradise had a population of 26,412 people.

Colloquially known as "Surfers", the suburb has many high-rise apartment buildings and a wide surf beach. The feature of the heart of the suburb is Cavill Mall, which runs through the shopping and entertainment precinct. Cavill Avenue, named after Jim Cavill, an early hotel owner, is one of the busiest shopping strips in Queensland, and the centre of activity for night life. One of the features of the area is the Surfers Paradise Meter Maids designed to build goodwill with tourists.

Surfers Paradise is the Gold Coast's entertainment and tourism centre and the suburb's high-rise buildings are the best known feature of the city's skyline. (Wikipedia)

ImageDescription.value:
I'm back everyone! Having enjoyed a week of R&R across the ditch on Australia's sunny Gold Coast I returned to Christchurch this afternoon to a miserable wet day and a temperature drop of about 20 degrees... Anyway, I thought I'd start off my Gold Coast car spots (of which there are quite a few!) with this completely car-free shot of the Surfers Paradise skyline, taken from a bridge on Monaco Street in the well-off suburb of Broadbeach Waters.

Most of the houses in the richer suburbs of the Gold Coast have their own beach and jetty, as in between most streets there are narrow waterways to launch your boat in. They all feed off the long Nerang River. Check out the map to see what I mean.

I'll upload some cars in the morning as it's late and I'm tired...

Photo taken at 3.49pm AEST, on October 7, 2012.
